page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench with a score of 2348.0, and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression at 34.74 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.17 GB/sec. However, due to its low core count, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with large-block read-only bandwidth measured at 21.36 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX8-2ms_v2 offers a specialized hardware profile that prioritizes massive memory capacity per vCPU over dense parallel processing power. This makes it a highly qualitative option for memory-intensive workloads that do not scale across many cores but require significant RAM, such as large in-memory caches, single-threaded data processing, or memory-bound database operations.
